rows.source: the object's own description: "indicates if we are locked on the carrier". Not locked is not a setting and not a degradation — there is no signal.

the critical point is the vendor's own: "a noise margin <=0 means that the signal is very likely to be undecodable" (ATEME-DR5000-MIB, dr5000StatusInputSatSnrMargin, in centibels). The 1.0 dB and 2.0 dB rungs above it are a SITE RULE — how much warning this plant wants before that happens — and are the two numbers to change per link and per dish.

ETSI TR 101 290 §5.2 quasi-error-free: BER after Viterbi at 2e-4 is the point at which the transport stream stops being QEF, which is 20000 in this object's own unit ("multiples of 1e-8", ATEME-DR5000-MIB). The minor rung at 2e-5 is one decade earlier — a SITE RULE for early warning.
the object's own unit is kbps; zero means nothing is arriving at all. Read 44350 on the live carrier (2026-09-23).
the object's own description: "indicates if there is a video on the output". This is the one an operator is actually paid to watch.
the object's own description: "defines either the following fields are valid or not" — when it is false, the codec/format fields beside it mean nothing, so a dashboard reading them is reading noise.
every other object the IRD defines (~26 000 of them, most in the programme tables); the model defines the view, these rules only colour it
